title: 51 Squadron RAF Memorial Garden, Pollington (RAF Snaith)
location_name: Heck and Pollington Lane, Pollington, East Riding of Yorkshire, DN14 0WG
aircraft_type: Handley Page Halifax Mks II and III
squadron_display_name: 51 Squadron RAF, 4 Group, Bomber Command (also 150 Squadron and 578 Squadron)
memorial_name: 51 Squadron RAF Memorial Garden and RAF Snaith Museum
memorial_address: Heck and Pollington Lane, Pollington, East Riding of Yorkshire, DN14 0WG
memorial_details: Purpose-built memorial garden on the footprint of the former RAF Snaith headquarters building. Features a stone of remembrance, approximately 100 individual crew plaques for crews who failed to return, trees, shrubs, and group memorials. Open 365 days a year. Biannual reunion services held in May and November. The adjacent RAF Snaith Museum (opened 2023) is housed on the former WAAF Site Number 1 and holds artefacts, records, and displays relating to 51 Squadron, 150 Squadron, 4 Group, and the Women's Land Army.
inscription: In memory of the 687 airmen of 51 Squadron, 4 Group, Bomber Command who lost their lives flying Halifax Bombers Marks II and III here at RAF Snaith between October 1942 and April 1945. Also remembering the 205 airmen of 150 Squadron lost on active duty who preceded them at this airfield flying Wellington Bombers Marks I and III.
crew_summary: 892 airmen commemorated in total: 687 of 51 Squadron and 205 of 150 Squadron. Garden contains approximately 100 individual crew plaques.
narrative:
RAF Snaith opened as a bomber station in 1941. 150 Squadron flew Wellingtons from the station before 51 Squadron arrived in October 1942 to convert to the Halifax. Over the following two and a half years 51 Squadron lost 687 aircrew — the highest casualty figure for any of the 19 stations at which the squadron was based across its history. 578 Squadron was formed from 51 Squadron's 'C' Flight at Snaith in January 1944 before moving to RAF Burn the following month.

Australian and New Zealand airmen are among those named on the individual plaques, reflecting the multinational composition of 4 Group's squadrons. The garden is managed as a living memorial with biannual reunion services attended by veterans' descendants and representatives of the modern RAF.

The RAF Snaith Museum, opened in 2023 on the adjacent former WAAF site, holds artefacts, records, and displays relating to 51 Squadron, 150 Squadron, 4 Group Bomber Command, and the Women's Land Army. The modern 51 Squadron — now a reconnaissance unit — maintains its connection to the Snaith memorial and has marked its anniversary there.
